title: One-Pan Lemon Orzo (25 Minutes, One Pan to Wash)
creator: Priya Bakes
description:
The weeknight dinner I make more than anything else: creamy lemon orzo with spinach and parmesan, all in one pan.

This video is sponsored by Hearthbox. Get 60% off your first box plus free shipping with code PRIYA60 at https://hearthbox.com/priya

RECIPE
1 shallot, 3 garlic cloves, 1.5 cups orzo, 3.5 cups warm stock, 2 lemons, 2 handfuls spinach, butter, parmesan, pine nuts, basil.

Instagram: @priyabakes

sentences.t: Hey everyone, welcome back to the kitchen.
Today we are making my one-pan lemon orzo, and I promise you it takes about twenty-five minutes start to finish.
Which, on a Tuesday, is about all the energy I have.
So first thing, get a wide pan going on medium heat with a good glug of olive oil.
I'm using a twelve-inch stainless pan, but honestly a nonstick works fine here too.
In goes one diced shallot and a pinch of salt.
You just want it soft, not brown, so keep it moving.
Okay, that smells amazing already.
Now three cloves of garlic, grated straight in.
Thirty seconds, tops, because burnt garlic is the enemy.
Next, the orzo goes in dry, about a cup and a half.
And here's the trick most recipes skip, you toast it.
Stir it around in the oil for two or three minutes until some of the pieces turn golden.
That gives you this nutty, almost popcorn-y flavor that makes the whole dish taste way more complicated than it is.
See how it's going a little tan at the edges?
That's what we want.
Now the liquid.
Three and a half cups of warm chicken stock, or veggie stock if you want to keep it vegetarian.
Pour it in slowly, it's going to hiss at you, that's fine.
Bring it up to a simmer and then turn it down low.
You're going to stir this every couple of minutes, kind of like a lazy risotto.
Not constantly, I'm not a monster.
While that's going, zest two lemons.
Get the zest only, not the white pith, because the pith is bitter.
And then juice them, and catch the seeds with your fingers like this.
Okay, it's been about ten minutes, let's check.
The orzo's almost tender, still a little bite in the middle, and most of the stock is absorbed.
This is where the spinach goes in, a big handful, maybe two.
It looks like way too much, it is not too much, it wilts down to nothing.
Then the lemon zest, the juice, and a knob of butter.
And a big handful of parmesan, like a really generous one.
Stir that until it goes glossy and creamy.
If it gets too thick, splash in a little more stock or some pasta water, whatever you've got.
Taste it.
Mm, okay, it needs more salt, it always needs more salt.
And a crack of black pepper.
I like to finish it with some toasted pine nuts and a few torn basil leaves on top.
Look at that.
Bright, creamy, a little bit cheesy, and literally one pan to wash.
If you want protein, this is great with a piece of seared salmon or some white beans stirred in at the end.
Leftovers keep about three days in the fridge, just loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat.
Alright, that is it for today.
Thank you so much for watching, and if you make this, tag me, I genuinely love seeing your versions.
I'll see you next week with something chocolate, I think.
Bye!
